entries.question: How can Fusion connect workflows beyond Workfront itself?
entries.answer: It provides connectors for other applications and ways to connect to services with public APIs.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: What is one possible Fusion automation involving a Workfront request queue?
entries.answer: A scenario could watch a queue and create template-based projects from requests; this is a possible design, not proof it is enabled in a particular organization.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: What does a scenario represent in Workfront Fusion?
entries.answer: A scenario represents a workflow that watches for data and performs configured actions to transfer or transform it.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: What is Adobe Workfront Fusion designed to do?
entries.answer: Fusion automates processes by linking actions within and between applications and services.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: Why should you distinguish project, task and issue information when interpreting Workfront reporting?
entries.answer: They represent different work objects, so the meaning of a record and its relationship to the project must be understood before drawing conclusions.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: How can you connect report evidence to a training project instead of relying on the report's total row count?
entries.answer: Locate matching project or work-record identifiers and explain how the displayed information relates to the training work.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: How does a dashboard differ from a report in Workfront?
entries.answer: A dashboard assembles reports and other supported views into one place rather than representing one report alone.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: What is the main purpose of a Workfront report?
entries.answer: A report presents selected Workfront record information so users can inspect and understand work.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: What evidence shows that a document-review exercise went beyond simply uploading a file?
entries.answer: The document/version is identifiable and the agreed review or approval decision is visible with its reviewer and relevant comments or date.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: Why should you confirm the review workflow rather than assume every Workfront deployment uses the same proofing viewer?
entries.answer: Storage and integration choices affect review capabilities; Adobe cloud storage can use Frame.io-based review rather than Workfront proofing.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: How does a document approval differ from a proof review?
entries.answer: Document approval records a decision on a file; proof review provides a review experience with markup and feedback tools.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: What is a document in the context of Workfront work records?
entries.answer: A document is a file associated with work context such as a project, task or issue.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: Why is a submission confirmation alone insufficient to demonstrate a request-routing exercise?
entries.answer: You must also inspect the resulting issue and verify its actual destination, responsibility and observed status.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: What can happen to a Workfront request after submission and triage?
entries.answer: It can be assigned for handling or converted to a task or project under the configured process; conversion is not automatic for every request.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: What role do queue topics and routing rules play in Workfront intake?
entries.answer: Queue topics classify requests, while configured routing rules help direct submitted work to the intended destination or owner.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: What does a Workfront request queue provide?
entries.answer: A request queue is a configured intake route for submitting unplanned work into Workfront.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: After creating a training project from a template, what should you inspect before assigning or progressing tasks?
entries.answer: Inspect copied tasks, assignments, dates and settings, then use the agreed training assignee and permitted lifecycle changes.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: How do planned hours differ from task duration?
entries.answer: Planned hours express expected effort; duration expresses the scheduled time span over which a task is planned.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: What kinds of information can a Workfront template transfer into a new project?
entries.answer: Template configuration can transfer tasks, assignments, durations, documents, custom forms and other project information.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: What is a Workfront project template used for?
entries.answer: A project template provides a reusable plan and settings that can be copied into a new project.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: Does seeing a Workfront menu or creation button prove you can edit every object in that area?
entries.answer: No. Relevant license/access capabilities and permissions on the specific object must also allow the action.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: Why might two Workfront users see different options in the Main Menu?
entries.answer: License type and assigned layout-template configuration can change the navigation options a user sees.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: Which Workfront navigation destination commonly organizes a user's daily work?
entries.answer: Home is the usual personal-work landing area, although an administrator can configure a different landing page.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: Which Workfront navigation control opens areas such as Projects, Requests and Reports?
entries.answer: The Main Menu provides navigation to the Workfront areas available to your account.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: Which Workfront objects can organize multiple projects for higher-level oversight?
entries.answer: Portfolios and programs group projects; programs can organize projects within a portfolio.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: Which Workfront object commonly tracks an incoming request or an unexpected problem?
entries.answer: An issue represents unplanned work such as an incoming request or problem within a project.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: Which Workfront object represents a planned unit of work within a project?
entries.answer: A task describes a planned work unit, with responsibility and progress tracked within its project.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)

entries.question: Which Workfront object organizes a planned outcome and holds its related tasks and issues?
entries.answer: A project is the work container for a planned outcome and its associated tasks and issues.
entries.class: Core Workfront Learnings and Hands-On Training Basics - Tracy (MRT-2134)
